title: FinLLM-KG: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment Analysis in Algorithmic Trading
summary: Recent advances in Generative AI have substantially improved financial sentiment analysis through post-trained financial large language models (LLMs). However, existing approaches remain confined to predicting the sentiment of each article in isolation and operate as black boxes, which limits contextual understanding and hinders deployment in high-stakes financial decision-making. To this end, we introduce FinLLM-KG, a model-agnostic framework that combines causal LLMs with a financial knowledge graph, in order to inject temporally grounded, company-level knowledge from SEC 10-K filings at inference time, without updating model weights. Within FinLLM-KG, context is supplied either as a natural-language company profile or as a small set of relevance-ranked factual triples. This enables sentiment predictions to account for broader firm-level information rather than the article alone, at almost zero computational cost and for any causal LLM. In addition, attributing each article-level sentiment score to individual sentences and to the retrieved knowledge-graph facts makes the evidence behind the prediction inspectable, thereby enhancing explainability and supporting human-in-the-loop review. Simulations demonstrate that FinLLM-KG consistently improves portfolio performance over the state-of-the-art baseline.
core_methodology: Combines causal large language models (LLMs) with a financial knowledge graph to enhance financial sentiment analysis by incorporating temporally grounded, company-level knowledge from SEC 10-K filings during inference, without updating model weights. The framework allows context to be supplied as natural-language company profiles or relevance-ranked factual triples, improving sentiment predictions and explainability.
data_sources: SEC 10-K filings (company-level financial disclosures) and financial news articles for sentiment analysis.
alpha_potential: The integration of company-specific knowledge from SEC filings with sentiment analysis allows for more informed and context-aware trading decisions. The explainability and attribution features support human-in-the-loop review, which can enhance trust and adoption in high-stakes trading environments. The paper demonstrates improved portfolio performance in simulations, suggesting potential alpha generation through better sentiment signal extraction.
title_cn: FinLLM-KG：用于算法交易中情感分析的知识图谱增强大语言模型
summary_cn: FinLLM-KG通过将因果大语言模型与金融知识图谱结合，利用SEC 10-K文件中的公司级知识增强情感分析，在推理时注入上下文信息。该方法显著提升情感预测的准确性，同时通过归因分析增强可解释性，支持人工复核。模拟测试表明，该框架能持续提升投资组合表现，适用于高频金融决策。

title: ATEMPO: Amortized Transfer Entropy Model Per-lag Over-Time
summary: When one time series informs another, the delay at which that information arrives determines if models can utilize this relationship effectively. A source may be strongly predictive at one delay but uninformative at neighboring lags. Therefore, fixed input windows may obscure this structure by bundling informative and irrelevant history together. Transfer entropy (TE) can recover these delays by measuring how much a source's past tells us about a target beyond the target's own history. However, existing TE estimators require separate fits across source and conditioning depths, with further estimation on local windows to track delays over time. We introduce ATEMPO, a diffusion-based transfer entropy estimator amortized over lags and time. ATEMPO samples source and conditioning depths during training and conditions explicitly on temporal position, allowing a single score network to estimate the full TE surface without refitting. Differencing this surface recovers when information arrives. Across synthetic datasets with ground-truth TE, ATEMPO achieves the lowest mean relative error among baselines, and on datasets with known lags, ATEMPO achieves $0.98\pm0.04$ lag-detection accuracy. ATEMPO requires a single fit across source depths $K=6$ and target depths $L=3$, whereas existing estimators require 18 separate fits to evaluate the same $K \times L$ grid. On three systems with time-varying lag, ATEMPO is the only estimator to maintain perfect lag-detection accuracy across all evaluated window lengths. These recovered delays improve downstream forecasting: ATEMPO-selected inputs reduce MSE on WEATHER-5K by 7.25%, while 120 selected inputs outperform the benchmark's 240-feature default by 4.6%. Across three brain-computer interface tasks, using ATEMPO-selected lags achieves the highest or equal-best $R^2$, improving mean $R^2$ by 4.1% relative to the strongest competing baseline.
core_methodology: ATEMPO introduces a diffusion-based transfer entropy estimator that is amortized over lags and time. It samples source and conditioning depths during training and conditions explicitly on temporal position, allowing a single score network to estimate the full transfer entropy surface without refitting. This method enables efficient detection of information arrival delays, which is particularly relevant for time-series forecasting.
data_sources: The paper evaluates ATEMPO on synthetic datasets with ground-truth transfer entropy, datasets with known lags, weather data (WEATHER-5K), and brain-computer interface tasks. The methodology is broadly applicable to financial time-series data, such as price, volume, or alternative data streams.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that ATEMPO-selected inputs improve forecasting accuracy, reducing MSE on weather data by 7.25% and outperforming benchmark models with fewer features. In financial applications, this could translate to better predictive models for asset returns or risk factors by more accurately identifying the optimal lags for informative features, leading to more efficient market timing strategies or improved risk management.
title_cn: ATEMPO：基于扩散模型的时滞感知转移熵估计方法
summary_cn: ATEMPO提出了一种基于扩散模型的转移熵估计方法，能够高效地检测信息传递的时滞。该方法通过单次训练即可估计完整的转移熵曲面，无需针对不同时滞重复拟合。在金融时序预测中，ATEMPO可帮助更准确地识别特征的最优滞后阶数，提升交易信号的预测精度。实验表明，该方法在误差降低和特征选择效率方面优于基准模型，明显提升了预测性能。

title: Timestral
summary: We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric. We achieve this with three ingredients: Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), which separates prediction tokens from the causally encoded context, so that longer horizons are trained without masking context and each observed value is both a forecast target and context for later forecasts; a covariate framework that natively supports known-future covariates within a causal architecture; and a two-stage pipeline that pretrains exclusively on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus before post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data with extended context. This report describes the model design and its benchmark results. Weights for all four models are available on Hugging Face and inference code on GitHub.
core_methodology: Timestral introduces a family of time series foundation models with Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), which separates prediction tokens from causally encoded context, and uses a covariate framework supporting known-future covariates within a causal architecture. The models are pretrained on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus before post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data.
data_sources: The models are pretrained on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus and then post-trained on a mix of real and synthetic data with extended context.
alpha_potential: Timestral's ability to handle probabilistic forecasting with high accuracy and efficiency, especially in scenarios involving known-future covariates, makes it highly applicable for trading strategies that rely on time-series predictions, such as momentum strategies, factor investing, and portfolio optimization. The model's state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks suggests strong potential for alpha generation.
title_cn: 时间序列基础模型家族Timestral
summary_cn: Timestral是一种用于概率预测的时间序列基础模型家族，通过分离预测标记和因果编码上下文，支持已知未来协变量的因果架构。其高精度预测能力使其在量化交易中具有广泛应用潜力，如动量策略、因子投资和组合优化。模型在基准测试中表现优异，显示出显著的阿尔法生成潜力。

title: Learning from Points and Patches: A Pre-trained Hybrid Attention Transformer for Time Series Analysis
summary: Time-series data generated by Web services and connected systems support applications such as user activity analysis, service monitoring, and resource management. However, learning transferable representations from heterogeneous time series remains challenging due to diverse temporal patterns, variable sequence lengths, and limited high-quality annotations. Despite the success of pre-training in natural language processing and computer vision, effective time-series pre-training requires strategies tailored to temporal data. We propose TimeHAT (Hybrid Attention Transformer), a general-purpose pre-training framework for time-series analysis that addresses two complementary questions: what to learn and how to learn. For what to learn, we introduce a Unified Point-Patch Masking Strategy (UPPMS) that integrates point-level and patch-level supervision within a unified framework for contextual reconstruction and causal extrapolation, enabling the model to capture both fine-grained temporal variations and broader temporal patterns. For how to learn, we develop a Hybrid Attention Encoder (HAE) that combines prefix-constrained bidirectional attention in initial layers with directional hybrid attention in deeper layers, aiming to preserve effective contextual interactions while mitigating rank degeneration. We evaluate TimeHAT across real-world datasets and four downstream tasks: classification, long-term forecasting, imputation, and anomaly detection. Experiments cover fine-tuning, few-shot, and zero-shot transfer settings, demonstrating competitive performance across diverse time-series analysis tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/TangPeiwang/TimeHAT.
core_methodology: TimeHAT (Hybrid Attention Transformer) with Unified Point-Patch Masking Strategy (UPPMS) for contextual reconstruction and causal extrapolation, combined with a Hybrid Attention Encoder (HAE) that integrates prefix-constrained bidirectional attention and directional hybrid attention.
data_sources: Real-world heterogeneous time-series data, potentially applicable to financial time-series data such as price movements, trading volumes, and other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to learn transferable representations from diverse temporal patterns and variable sequence lengths is promising for financial applications, especially in areas like forecasting, anomaly detection, and imputation of missing market data.
title_cn: 从点和块中学习：用于时间序列分析的预训练混合注意力Transformer
summary_cn: 该研究提出的TimeHAT框架通过混合注意力机制和点块统一掩码策略，能够有效捕捉金融时间序列中的细粒度变动和宏观模式，适用于市场预测、异常检测及数据填补等交易场景。在少样本和零样本迁移设置下表现优异，为量化交易中的时序分析提供了新工具。

title: Gaussian Process Bandits for Constraint Black Box Lever Optimization
summary: Optimizing discrete allocation weights across competing segments of a shared budget is a fundamental challenge in resource-constrained, sequential decision-making environments. In practice, this optimization is often hindered by delayed, noisy, and aggregate feedback, alongside strict operational constraints on how frequently weights can be adjusted. Because of the resulting combinatorial action space and extreme data sparsity, classical multi-armed bandit algorithms that evaluate arms independently are rendered highly inefficient. To overcome these limitations, we propose a segmentation-agnostic approach utilizing Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (GP-UCB) algorithms. By placing a Gaussian Process prior on the reward function, our method effectively shares information across neighboring configurations, drastically reducing the necessary exploration horizon. In this paper, we bridge the gap between theoretical bandit research and production-scale deployment. We first introduce a high-fidelity synthetic simulator to evaluate various kernel configurations under stationary, drifting, and reactive environments, identifying a composite Mat\'ern + Linear kernel as the most robust choice for overcoming local noise and global shifts. Finally, we validate our findings through a large-scale Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) in a live production environment. Our empirical results demonstrate that the GP-UCB approach delivers a statistically significant efficiency lift compared to a standard $\varepsilon$-greedy baseline, offering a highly practical solution for real-world black-box lever optimization.
core_methodology: Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (GP-UCB) algorithms applied to combinatorial optimization of discrete allocation weights under noisy and delayed feedback conditions
data_sources: Operational data from production systems (field tested via RCT), synthetic simulator with stationary/drifting/reactive environments
alpha_potential: Potential for dynamic portfolio weight optimization under market regime changes, efficient exploration of strategy parameter spaces in trading systems with execution constraints
title_cn: 基于高斯过程赌博机的约束黑盒杠杆优化
summary_cn: 该研究提出将高斯过程上置信界算法应用于资源受限环境下的组合权重优化，通过信息共享机制大幅提升探索效率。通过复合核函数处理市场噪声和全局漂移，在实盘RCT中显示统计显著的绩效提升，可直接应用于交易策略参数优化和动态组合管理场景。

title: LiveSearch: Questions as Executable Verifier Code for a Live Benchmark of Professional-Source Financial Search Agents
summary: In finance, the answer that matters is usually the current one: prices, rates, and disclosures hold only as of a given day, so retrieving up-to-date facts is a core capability of a financial agent. Yet most financial benchmarks overlook timeliness. They fix each answer at annotation time, so the gold goes stale as markets move and, once leaked into training data, rewards recall rather than search and analysis. We introduce LiveSearch, a live benchmark that stores each question as executable verifier code: a typed program of calls to a professional financial data service, followed by a declarative extractor. The question is frozen, while its gold answer is determined by executing the program against professional financial data at evaluation time, and a daily job re-executes it with no human or language model in the loop. A memorized answer is thus likely outdated, and a model must reach the current one through tools and analysis. Construction is equally automatic: a language model only verbalizes programs enumerated from real tool responses and never chooses an answer. Under general web search, six contemporary tool-calling models reach 70.9% to 76.7% answer accuracy. Over three consecutive days, 70% of served questions change their gold value, and even under tolerance-aware matching, a literally reused earlier snapshot fails on a majority of questions within a single day. Per-question tracking uncovers dynamic shifts in correctness masked by aggregate accuracy.
core_methodology: LiveSearch stores each question as executable verifier code, which is a typed program that calls a professional financial data service to retrieve current data. The benchmark ensures answers are up-to-date by re-executing the program daily against professional financial data without human intervention, thus enforcing the use of tools and analysis rather than memorization.
data_sources: Professional financial data services providing up-to-date prices, rates, and disclosures.
alpha_potential: The methodology encourages the development of financial agents that dynamically retrieve and analyze current financial data, which can lead to better-informed trading decisions by avoiding reliance on stale information. This is particularly relevant for high-frequency trading and day trading where current data is crucial.
title_cn: LiveSearch：问题作为可执行验证代码用于实时专业金融搜索代理基准测试
summary_cn: LiveSearch是一种实时基准测试方法，将每个问题存储为可执行的验证代码，通过调用专业金融数据服务动态获取最新数据，确保答案的实时性。这种方法避免了依赖陈旧数据，可直接应用于高频交易和日内交易，提高决策的时效性和准确性。

title: Strategyproof Deep Reinforcement Learning for Online Resource Allocation
summary: Online resource allocation faces two coupled challenges: (1) allocating scarce resources efficiently under uncertain future demand, and (2) ensuring that agents report task valuations and requirements truthfully (strategyproofness). Reinforcement Learning (RL) adapts allocation decisions through experience but does not necessarily ensure strategyproofness. Existing strategyproof RL uses a linear allocation rule, which limits the resource interactions it can represent. Neural mechanism design methods offer greater expressiveness, but provide only approximate incentive guarantees. Against this background, we introduce the first strategyproof deep RL mechanism for online resource allocation. It integrates three novel components: (i) a monotonic neural network that learns nonlinear interactions by construction (higher reported value cannot reduce acceptance, while a longer reported duration or larger resource requirement cannot increase it); (ii) a generalised critical payment: the lowest accepted value, with all other inputs fixed; and (iii) training by either RL or imitation of an existing rule. Together, monotonicity and the critical payment ensure strategyproofness and individual rationality, while the neural rule provides flexibility and imitation improves training efficiency. Empirically, on a four-resource stream with two partner pairs that a linear difference cannot represent, the neural rule achieves 97.8% of an offline welfare upper bound, compared with 93.8% for a linear learner and 89.0% for first-come, first-served, closing 65% and 80% of the remaining optimality gap, respectively. Moreover, imitation reaches 97.5% in only 261 seconds, about 89 times faster than RL.
core_methodology: Strategyproof deep reinforcement learning with monotonic neural networks and critical payments for online resource allocation
data_sources: Simulated resource allocation scenarios with uncertain demand patterns (abstract describes a four-resource stream with two partner pairs)
alpha_potential: Potential applications in dynamic capital allocation, execution algorithms, or crypto/fintech where truthful reporting and efficient allocation are critical. The 97.8% welfare achievement vs. benchmarks (93.8% linear learner) shows promise for market-making/asset allocation problems.
title_cn: 面向在线资源分配的策略性深度强化学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出首个策略性深度强化学习机制，通过单调神经网络和关键支付确保资源分配中的真实性，在模拟测试中达到离线上限97.8%的福利水平。该算法可应用于高频交易中的资金动态分配、加密货币做市等需要高效且防操纵的金融场景，其非线性交互建模能力超越传统线性方法。

title: Beyond Greenwashing: Algorithmic Resilience and the Non-Linear Governance Premium in Sovereign Capital Flows
summary: Despite the proliferation of sovereign Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) metrics, traditional linear macro-financial models systematically misprice Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) tail risks during systemic shocks. This paper demonstrates that sovereign risk transmission is fundamentally non-linear. Using a forward-chained global panel of 147 sovereign entities (2010-2024), we deploy a gradient boosting architecture that compresses forecast errors by over 39% against L1-regularized baselines precisely during extreme macroeconomic tail events. Moving beyond opaque predictive accuracy, we apply dual interpretability frameworks to mathematically map the discrete threshold effects of institutional quality. We identify a strict, non-linear "Governance Premium": incremental environmental and social improvements yield zero capital advantage until a foundational regulatory threshold is breached. Finally, we establish regime-conditional 95% uncertainty bounds that maintain valid marginal coverage even under severe ESG reporting failures. This framework equips policymakers with a distribution-free tool to quantify sovereign tail-risk, proving that global capital markets price institutional resilience as a discrete boundary rather than a continuous premium.
core_methodology: Gradient boosting architecture for non-linear sovereign risk modeling with interpretability frameworks to identify threshold effects in governance quality.
data_sources: Global panel of 147 sovereign entities from 2010 to 2024, focusing on Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and institutional quality metrics.
alpha_potential: Identifies a non-linear 'Governance Premium' where incremental ESG improvements have zero capital advantage until a regulatory threshold is breached, providing a potential signal for sovereign risk pricing and tail-risk management.
title_cn: 超越表面绿化：算法韧性及主权资本流动中的非线性治理溢价
summary_cn: 本文通过梯度提升架构和可解释性框架，揭示了主权风险传输的非线性特性，识别出只有当监管阈值被突破时，环境和社会改善才会带来资本优势的‘治理溢价’。这一发现为量化主权尾部风险及优化全球资本配置提供了新的交易策略视角。

title: QD-PINN:A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions
summary: Quickest detection problems (QDPs) arise in a wide range of applications. However, the complementarity structure of the associated variational inequalities poses substantial challenges for traditional numerical methods, particularly in high-dimensional settings. We propose a PINN-based framework for estimating the optimal stopping boundary in QDPs with high-dimensional diffusion processes and spatial dependence, while overcoming the curse of dimensionality. Theoretically, we establish a novel equivalence between the free-boundary PDE and an infinite-dimensional stochastic optimization problem, rigorously justifying the use of finite-dimensional neural networks to approximate the true solution. Furthermore, we assess the robustness of the proposed framework by quantifying uncertainty in the learned stopping boundaries using deep ensembles and Monte Carlo dropout. The results show low variability across independent training runs and stochastic forward passes, indicating stable and consistent boundary estimates. We also compare our PINN results with reference numerical solutions where available and find close agreement.
core_methodology: Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework for solving high-dimensional quickest detection problems (QDPs), incorporating Bayesian uncertainty quantification through deep ensembles and Monte Carlo dropout
data_sources: High-dimensional diffusion processes, potentially applicable to financial time series and multivariate asset pricing models
alpha_potential: Enables optimized early detection of regime changes or anomaly events in complex market conditions, potentially improving timing of tactical asset allocation or crisis detection
title_cn: 基于物理信息神经网络的贝叶斯快速检测方法在高维扩散过程中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合物理信息神经网络(PINN)与贝叶斯方法的框架,专门用于解决高维扩散过程中的快速检测问题,在时序分析和多重资产定价场景下具有潜在应用价值。该框架通过随机优化实现了维数灾难的突破,并使用深度集成方法量化边界估计的不确定性,可为市场状态转变检测提供更可靠的定量工具。

title: Hedge-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks Pertaining to Financial Reasoning
summary: Modern AI agents are increasingly capable of routine financial-analysis tasks such as retrieving documents and updating spreadsheets. A harder challenge is forecasting an unknown future from incomplete information. Public markets provide a natural testbed: analysts routinely predict discrete events with information from that point in time. We present Hedge-Bench, a benchmark of 92 real-world environments derived from hedge fund analysts' reasoning traces paired with subsequently resolved prediction questions. Agents reason from frozen information snapshots, and their forecasts are evaluated against real-world outcomes. Across 11 frontier models and three trials per environment, joint success rates, which require both a correct forecast and over 60% research coverage, range from 2.54 to 31.52%. Using GRPO with turn-level credit assignment, we train Muse-Glimmer on 165 environments, increasing coverage on 22 held-out environments from 17.17% to 33.36% at low reasoning effort and from 30.19% to 47.02% at extra-high effort. The trained model at low effort also exceeds the base model's extra-high-effort coverage while using 47.9% fewer tokens. We also observe evidence of generalization: held-out forecasting accuracy at high effort improves by 10.06 percentage points, while out-of-distribution evaluation scores improve by 3.94 points on GDPval, 2.29 on GDP.pdf, 7.07 on Harvey LAB, and 4.96 on Frontier Finance under their respective metrics. Code: https://github.com/Trata-Inc/trata-hedge-bench-verified.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Hedge-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on financial reasoning tasks using real-world hedge fund analysts' reasoning traces. It employs GRPO (likely a reinforcement learning method) with turn-level credit assignment to train models like Muse-Glimmer, improving forecast accuracy and research coverage.
data_sources: Real-world environments derived from hedge fund analysts' reasoning traces, paired with resolved prediction questions. The data includes frozen information snapshots and real-world outcomes for evaluation.
alpha_potential: The methodology demonstrates potential for improving forecast accuracy and research coverage in financial markets, which could lead to better investment decisions. The trained model reduces token usage while maintaining or improving performance, indicating efficiency gains.
title_cn: Hedge-Bench：在关于金融推理的困难和现实任务上对代理进行基准测试
summary_cn: 该论文提出了Hedge-Bench基准，基于对冲基金分析师的实际推理轨迹来评估AI代理在金融预测任务上的表现。通过GRPO和逐轮信用分配训练Muse-Glimmer模型，显著提高了预测准确性和研究覆盖率，同时减少了计算资源消耗，对量化投资中的决策支持系统具有实际应用价值。

title: Simple Portfolios that Deliver Consistent Decent Returns
summary: Portfolio construction has been studied extensively in both academia and industry. Its applications range from pension funds and hedge funds to private savings. The academic literature centers on methodology, commonly evaluated in settings that allow short selling, leverage, and frequent trading. Industry, on the other hand, operates under real constraints, but its data and methods are proprietary and largely unpublished. Neither is directly available to the private investor. This paper is an empirical study of established portfolio construction methods in the setting of the private investor. We consider a small investable universe of liquid US ETFs, where trading is monthly and carries a cost, and neither shorting nor leverage is permitted. Portfolio construction is posed as a convex optimization problem, its inputs are estimated from public data, and every parameter is interpretable. We denote such portfolios simple. We show that simple portfolios of as few as three ETFs deliver consistent and decent returns, without tuning to the backtest period. To find them, we have developed a framework, which we share publicly, able to backtest hundreds of portfolios on a standard laptop over a twenty year period or longer. When no return forecast is made, portfolios are constructed from risk alone, using methods such as risk parity and minimum volatility, built on a statistical factor model fitted with expectation maximization. When a forecast is made, we combine the Markowitz formulation with momentum signals and ridge regression. We report what works and what each component adds, weighing its gain against its complexity and the effort it demands of the investor. The findings are supported by numerical experiments over the past two decades, and the proposed portfolios outperform the standard 60/40 allocation.
core_methodology: Portfolio construction framed as a convex optimization problem, incorporating risk parity, minimum volatility, and momentum signals with ridge regression. Uses statistical factor models fitted via expectation maximization.
data_sources: Public data on liquid US ETFs, covering at least 20 years of historical data.
alpha_potential: Demonstrates consistent outperformance versus 60/40 benchmark through systematic risk allocation and momentum integration, particularly in constrained settings (no leverage/shorting). The statistical factor model may capture latent risk premia.
title_cn: 能带来持续稳定收益的简单投资组合构建策略
summary_cn: 本研究在个人投资者约束条件下（无杠杆/做空），通过凸优化框架结合风险平价、最小波动率等经典方法及动量信号，构建仅需3只ETF的组合。公开的回测系统验证了其20年持续跑赢60/40基准的能力，为零售投资者提供了机构级配置工具。

title: Depositing More Should Not Earn Less: Supplier Income Monotonicity and Rate Curve Design in Pooled Lending Markets
summary: In utilization dependent interest rate models, adding liquidity can reduce a supplier's total interest income even as the supplier's balance increases. A supplier holding a fraction $\alpha$ of final pool supply keeps income nondecreasing with a marginal deposit exactly when $\alpha(1+\eta)\leq1$, where $\eta$ is the elasticity of the borrow rate with respect to utilization. When the condition fails, the supplier can instead raise its income by withdrawing, which pushes utilization further up. On two public Drift markets, a lender held more of the pool than the curve protected in at least one hour in nine on SOL and one in thirteen on USDC. A protocol turns this into a design constraint by choosing, at each utilization, the largest supplier share it intends to protect. That choice caps the elasticity, and integrating the cap describes every admissible curve. Protecting the same share at every utilization gives a power law boundary, and protecting every fresh depositor gives a hyperbolic one. On a multiple kink USDT market, compliant repairs can lower or raise supplier income, because the constraint governs how income responds to a deposit and not the price level.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes utilization-dependent interest rate models in pooled lending markets, focusing on the conditions under which a supplier's income remains nondecreasing with marginal deposits. It introduces mathematical constraints (α(1+η)≤1) to ensure income monotonicity and proposes rate curve designs (power law and hyperbolic boundaries) based on these constraints.
data_sources: The study uses public data from Drift markets, specifically analyzing SOL and USDC lending pools, as well as a multiple kink USDT market.
alpha_potential: The paper identifies inefficiencies in pooled lending markets where suppliers can inadvertently reduce their income by adding liquidity. The proposed rate curve designs could help optimize supplier income, offering potential alpha in decentralized finance (DeFi) lending strategies by aligning deposit incentives with income maximization.
title_cn: 存款越多不应赚得越少：借贷池市场中的供应商收入单调性与利率曲线设计
summary_cn: 本文研究了借贷池市场中利用率依赖的利率模型，揭示了供应商收入随存款增加的单调性条件（α(1+η)≤1），并提出了相应的利率曲线设计（幂律和双曲线边界）。该研究为DeFi借贷策略提供了优化供应商收入的实用方法，可用于提高流动性提供者的收益。基于公开的Drift市场数据验证了理论的适用性。

title: Optimal Order Placement under a State-Dependent Hawkes Process Limit Order Book model
summary: We study optimal quote placement for a market maker facing order flow modeled by a state-dependent Hawkes process. A block-based linear demand specification links market-order counts to execution volumes, providing the demand moments required by a continuous time discrete state dynamic programming formulation. Under a quadratic terminal inventory penalty, we characterize inventory-dependent quotes and derive backward recursions for the coefficients of a quadratic value function. Numerical experiments using LOBSTER data examine quote distributions, inventory exposure, and terminal wealth. The implemented strategy yields higher aggregate terminal wealth than fixed-spread benchmarks at one and three ticks, but lower wealth than the two-tick benchmark. These results illustrate the framework's numerical implementation and distinguish terminal-wealth comparisons from evaluation under the inventory-penalized objective.
core_methodology: The paper employs a state-dependent Hawkes process for modeling order flow and uses a continuous time discrete state dynamic programming approach to solve the optimal quote placement problem for market makers.
data_sources: LOBSTER data, which provides detailed limit order book information.
alpha_potential: The method allows market makers to optimize their quotes dynamically based on inventory levels and market conditions, potentially capturing better execution prices and reducing adverse selection.
title_cn: 基于状态依赖霍克斯过程的限价订单簿模型下的最优订单配置
summary_cn: 该研究利用状态依赖霍克斯过程模拟订单流，并结合离散状态动态规划方法，为做市商提供最优报价策略。通过LOBSTER数据验证，该策略在一档和三档价位上表现优于固定点差基准，展现了动态报价策略在优化做市商绩效方面的潜力。

title: Market Regime-Based Multi-Asset Portfolio Optimization Using Nested Clustered Optimization for Tactical Asset Allocation
summary: We investigate the interaction between market regime detection and Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) for tactical asset allocation across heterogeneous multi asset portfolios. The central empirical question is whether conditioning the NCO pipeline, encompassing covariance estimation, hierarchical clustering, and weight allocation, on latent market states genuinely enhances risk adjusted performance, or conversely, whether estimation uncertainty within regime filtered sub samples induces severe turnover and performance drag. We implement a causal rolling Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) coupled with an adaptive rebalancing mechanism that distinguishes regime shifts from portfolio weight drift. The framework is evaluated on a monthly Indonesian multi asset universe comprising sovereign bond yields (SBN), the LQ45 equity index, spot gold (XAU/IDR), foreign exchange (CNY/IDR), and Bitcoin (BTC/IDR) across a 56 month out of sample period (January 2021 to August 2025). Rigorous walk forward backtesting reveals that standard regime agnostic NCO achieves remarkable capital preservation and risk adjusted efficiency, delivering a 29.97% cumulative return (5.78% annualized), a maximum drawdown of only 2.18%, a Calmar ratio of 2.65, and low monthly turnover of 5.41%. In contrast, conditioning NCO on an unconstrained HMM in a small multi asset universe amplifies parameter estimation noise and induces excessive rebalancing (47 events; 24.58% average monthly turnover), which erodes net cumulative return to 1.60% and increases drawdown to 9.99%. These findings demonstrate that without explicit transition persistence or asymmetric downside objectives, regime switching frameworks can degrade rather than improve clustered portfolio stability, establishing crucial empirical boundaries for machine learning asset allocation.
core_methodology: Combines Gaussian Hidden Markov Models (HMM) for market regime detection with Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) for portfolio optimization, implemented with adaptive rebalancing to distinguish regime shifts from weight drift.
data_sources: Monthly data from Indonesian multi-asset universe: sovereign bond yields (SBN), LQ45 equity index, spot gold (XAU/IDR), foreign exchange (CNY/IDR), and Bitcoin (BTC/IDR) from January 2021 to August 2025.
alpha_potential: Potential alpha from regime-aware asset allocation, though paper finds standard NCO performs better due to reduced turnover and parameter noise. Highlights importance of transition persistence and downside objectives in regime-switching models.
title_cn: 基于市场体制的多资产组合优化：使用嵌套聚类优化进行战术资产配置
summary_cn: 本研究探索了市场体制识别与嵌套聚类优化(NCO)在战术资产配置中的交互作用。实证发现，在印度尼西亚多资产组合中，标准NCO策略展现出卓越的资本保全和风险调整效率(年化5.78%)，而基于HMM的体制转换模型反而因过度调仓导致绩效下降。研究为机器学习在资产配置中的应用划定了重要实证边界。

title: Certifying Reward Alignment in Portfolio Reinforcement Learning
summary: Financial reinforcement learning often translates an investment objective into an additive risk-adjusted reward. An agent can optimise that reward accurately yet implement a different financial preference. We develop a decision audit for terminal mean-variance equilibrium that separates reward misspecification from learning error. In a finite exogenous-state market, we bound the gain from changing one action using actor, reward and continuation-critic residuals. The certificate ignores state-constant critic offsets, accommodates convex action constraints, and has an independent-sample extension that does not require the equilibrium policy. A continuation-aware actor-critic method estimates the future-policy correction from samples. Across nine controlled markets and twenty seeds, it reduces policy distance by and one-step deviation gain by relative to a matched myopic-reward network. A separate PPO comparison tests the same reward intervention within a standard optimiser. Historical tests cross seven covariance estimators and 10, 30 and 49 US industry portfolios over 432 months: joint reward calibration preserves each fitted mean-variance target, but does not improve realised investment performance. Together, these results provide a way to quantify whether a learned decision implements its stated financial objective, separately from how well that objective performs in a backtest.
core_methodology: The paper develops a decision audit framework for terminal mean-variance equilibrium in reinforcement learning (RL) applied to portfolio management. It introduces a certificate to distinguish between reward misspecification and learning errors, using actor-critic methods with continuation-aware corrections.
data_sources: The study uses controlled markets (nine settings with twenty seeds for validation) and real-world data from US industry portfolios (10, 30, and 49 portfolios) over 432 months with seven covariance estimators.
alpha_potential: The methodology provides a systematic way to ensure that learned policies align with stated financial objectives, which could improve the reliability of RL-based portfolio strategies. However, real-world tests showed it preserves mean-variance targets without improving realized performance, suggesting it's more valuable for validation than alpha generation.
title_cn: 投资组合强化学习中的奖励对齐认证
summary_cn: 本研究开发了一个用于终端均值-方差均衡的决策审计框架，区分奖励设定错误与学习误差。通过持续感知的演员-评论家方法，该方法在控制市场中有效减少策略偏差，但在实际行业组合测试中仅保持目标而未提升实盘表现。对验证RL策略与财务目标的对齐具有实用价值。

title: Jaxnasium: Embracing PyTrees For Any-Agent, Cross-Suite Reinforcement Learning
summary: Hardware-accelerated reinforcement learning in JAX has gained rapid popularity in recent years and has proven to be a successful method of scaling online reinforcement learning. The resulting ecosystem, however, is fragmented: environment suites define their own interfaces, and algorithm implementations are typically written for a single suite, a single type of space, and either JAX-native or host-based environments. Here we present Jaxnasium, a library for JAX-based reinforcement learning, aiming to make the field more accessible. Jaxnasium represents observation and action spaces as PyTrees, and uses this structure to build networks and support multi-agent processing. Through this, its near-single-file implementations run on discrete, continuous, image, and composite spaces, as well as in multi-agent environments, without any changes to the algorithm code. The same files serve as readable, research-friendly algorithms, as well as importable algorithms for more applied workloads. Through a minimal Gymnasium-style interface and wrappers for 11 suites, over 300 environments are available on which a small PPO implementation with default hyperparameters is able to run. Additionally, through a simple wrapper, we can run Gymnasium and EnvPool environments with the same algorithm and training loop, with no performance loss compared to architectures specifically built for training JAX algorithms on host-based environments. Jaxnasium further provides tools for multi-seed evaluation, hyperparameter sweeps, and project scaffolding. Jaxnasium is open-sourced at https://github.com/ponseko/jaxnasium
core_methodology: Jaxnasium is a JAX-based reinforcement learning library that uses PyTrees to represent observation and action spaces, enabling flexible algorithm implementations that can run across diverse environment types including discrete, continuous, image, and multi-agent spaces.
data_sources: Not specified in the abstract, but potentially applicable to any reinforcement learning environment, including simulated financial markets or real-time trading data streams.
alpha_potential: The library's generalizability and support for multi-agent environments could be leveraged to develop and test reinforcement learning-based trading strategies in diverse market conditions and across different asset classes. However, the abstract does not demonstrate specific financial applications.
title_cn: Jaxnasium：拥抱PyTrees实现任意智能体、跨套件的强化学习
summary_cn: Jaxnasium是一个基于JAX的强化学习库，通过PyTrees实现观察和动作空间的统一表示，能够开发跨多种环境类型的交易策略算法。其多智能体支持特性对开发复杂的量化交易策略系统具有潜在价值，但需结合具体金融数据验证应用效果。

title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
summary: Financial institutions operating under data-residency constraints are restricted to open-weight models small enough to locally host, which trail frontier systems on multi-step quantitative reasoning. On-policy distillation narrows such gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts, but traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. We ask how much of that signal is necessary. We present Fin-SD, a localized hindsight self-distillation recipe for multi-step reasoning. Given a problem the student fails, the student itself identifies the first incorrect reasoning step and writes a short critique of that step. We truncate the student's trajectory immediately before the error (aiming to obtain a correct prefix), condition a frozen copy of the student on the same prefix plus the hint, and distill that hint-conditioned teacher into the student over a short rollout under reverse KL. No external model contributes a gradient. We apply Fin-SD to GPT-OSS-20B on a custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark that requires deriving formula inputs from realistic scenarios via accounting conventions. We find: (i) replacing the critique with a generic-feedback control matches Fin-SD's entire 3.03 pp accuracy gain over the base model on the FinanceReasoning Hard subset, suggesting the gain comes from where supervision is applied, not hint content; (ii) the model writing the hint does not need to be stronger than the model receiving it: hints from same-family GPT-OSS-120B, at roughly 6x the parameters, yield no materially greater benefits than self-written hints; and (iii) Fin-SD matches on-policy self-distillation from full reference solutions on accuracy while generating 9.5% fewer tokens. With Fin-SD, general reasoning on MMLU-Pro and a fourteen-metric compliance audit on FinTrust show no material regression.
core_methodology: Fin-SD (hindsight self-distillation) for improving multi-step quantitative reasoning in financial applications by having a model self-correct its reasoning errors without external supervision
data_sources: Custom multi-step financial reasoning benchmark requiring formula derivation from realistic scenarios via accounting conventions
alpha_potential: Potential to enhance performance of locally-hosted models in quantitative reasoning tasks where data residency constraints prohibit using external APIs, applicable to financial statement analysis and quantitative risk modeling
title_cn: 提示信息有多重要？金融推理中后见自我蒸馏的范围条件
summary_cn: 本研究提出的Fin-SD方法通过自我蒸馏优化开源大模型在受限环境下的多步金融推理能力，无需外部监督，特别适用于受数据本地化限制的金融机构。该方法可提升财务比率计算、风险建模等定量分析质量，且不增加合规风险。

title: Dirichlet Process Mixtures within Semiparametric Bayesian Networks: A Novel Conditional Density Estimation Approach
summary: Semiparametric Bayesian networks (SPBNs) are flexible probabilistic graphical models for representing joint distributions of continuous variables through lower-dimensional conditional probability distributions (CPDs). Existing SPBN models use kernel density estimators (KDEs) for non-parametric CPD modeling, but their one-component-per-observation mixture representation can lead to increased inference costs and density estimation errors, which can be limiting. In this work, we define a new CPD modeling approach for non-parametric components based on Bayesian non-parametric Dirichlet Process Mixtures (DPMs) within SPBNs. DPMs provide a data-adaptive clustering of observations, yielding a more compact representation while retaining the flexibility of non-parametric density estimation, unlike KDE. This results in lower inference costs while improving density estimation performance. We implement the proposed DPM-based SPBN (DPM-SPBN) by extending the open-source PyBNesian package and evaluate it on synthetic and real-world data. For a given network structure, DPM-based CPDs significantly outperform state-of-the-art Bayesian network models for continuous variables in density estimation, achieving lower absolute log-likelihood errors on synthetic data. We further investigate the impact of the proposed CPD modeling on structure learning methods relying on CPD-based scores. DPM-based SPBNs achieve lower structure learning and density estimation errors than KDE-based SPBNs. Experiments on real-world data corroborate these findings, identifying DPM-based CPD modeling as the most effective alternative among the evaluated non-parametric approaches for continuous variables.
core_methodology: Dirichlet Process Mixtures (DPMs) within Semiparametric Bayesian Networks for conditional density estimation of continuous variables, offering more compact and accurate representations than traditional Kernel Density Estimators (KDEs).
data_sources: Synthetic data and real-world data (specific type not mentioned in the abstract).
alpha_potential: Potential for improved density estimation in financial modeling, such as probabilistic forecasts for asset returns or risk assessments, though direct trading application would require further development.
title_cn: 半参数贝叶斯网络中的Dirichlet过程混合：一种新的条件密度估计方法
summary_cn: 本研究引入了一种基于Dirichlet过程混合（DPM）的半参数贝叶斯网络（SPBN）方法，用于连续变量的条件密度估计。相较于传统的核密度估计（KDE），DPM-SPBN提供了更紧凑的数据表示和更高的估计精度，降低了推理成本。该方法在金融领域可能应用于资产收益的概率预测和风险评估，为量化模型提供更准确的密度估计基础。

title: Bayesian Evidence Accumulation for Graph-Based Learning in Dynamic Data-Driven Applications Systems
summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are widely used in modern machine learning, yet most existing frameworks remain fundamentally static, limiting their applicability in Dynamic Data Driven Application Systems (DDDAS) where observations arrive sequentially under uncertainty. We introduce B-EAGLe (Bayesian Evidence Accumulation for Graph-Based Learning), a probabilistic framework inspired by CBGT-Net (cortico-basal ganglia-thalamic network) that reformulates graph classification as a sequential evidence accumulation process. B-EAGLe combines a GNN encoder with a Bayesian accumulator that incrementally updates posterior beliefs over class labels as new observations arrive, committing to a decision only when sufficient confidence is achieved. Experiments on CIFAR10 demonstrate competitive performance together with principled confidence estimation under sequential observations.
core_methodology: B-EAGLe combines Graph Neural Networks (GNN) with a Bayesian accumulator to perform sequential evidence accumulation for graph classification under uncertainty. The framework incrementally updates posterior beliefs over class labels as new observations arrive, making decisions only when sufficient confidence is achieved.
data_sources: The paper demonstrates experiments on CIFAR10, which is a standard image dataset. However, the methodology could be adapted to financial time-series or graph-structured market data.
alpha_potential: The sequential evidence accumulation approach could be valuable for real-time decision-making in trading, such as detecting regime changes or momentum shifts in asset prices. The Bayesian framework provides principled confidence estimates, which could be useful for risk management.
title_cn: 基于贝叶斯证据积累的动态数据驱动应用系统中图学习的算法
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种在动态不确定性环境下实时更新决策的图学习方法，其核心在于贝叶斯置信度积累机制。对于量化交易的价值在于：1) 可用于市场状态识别的渐进式学习 2) 提供可靠的置信度指标以优化仓位数控制。特别适合处理高频数据流和非结构化市场关系数据。

title: AHEAD: Adaptive Neural Acceleration for Large-Scale Linear Programming
summary: Large-scale linear programs with millions of variables and constraints strain time and memory budgets. First-order methods such as the primal-dual hybrid gradient scale to this regime because they avoid matrix factorizations, but they require many iterations. Learned accelerators can reduce these iterations, yet fewer iterations do not guarantee a shorter solve. Learning inference also takes time, and running the accelerator longer trades solver time for inference time. Existing unrolled accelerators handle this trade-off poorly: each layer processes every variable and constraint, the predicted iterates still need solver refinement, and every instance runs the same layers. We therefore ask: What neural accelerator design achieves end-to-end speedups on large-scale linear programs across sizes and target accuracies? We introduce AHEAD, an accelerator that predicts step sizes for first-order linear programming solvers while keeping their update rules. Its weight-shared predictor reads compact solver statistics and rescales the primal and dual step sizes, so each warm-start iteration stays inexpensive and a short warm-start phase hands the solver a warm start. A learned handoff policy sets the number of warm-start iterations for each instance and target accuracy, after which the solver finishes under its own termination criterion. On packing linear programs with up to $10^7$ variables, AHEAD achieves $6.5$--$11.6\times$ end-to-end speedups over Gurobi's first-order solver from a cold start, including on instances of unseen sizes and distributions. The gains extend to PageRank linear programs and hold across difficulty levels and target accuracies.
core_methodology: AHEAD introduces a neural accelerator that predicts step sizes for first-order linear programming solvers, improving efficiency in solving large-scale linear programs. It uses compact solver statistics to rescale primal and dual step sizes, reducing the number of iterations needed.
data_sources: The paper does not explicitly specify financial data sources, focusing instead on solving linear programs commonly used in quantitative finance tasks like portfolio optimization.
alpha_potential: Potential to significantly reduce computational time in portfolio optimization, risk management, and other quantitative finance tasks involving large-scale linear programming, thereby enabling faster decision-making and higher frequency optimization.
title_cn: AHEAD: 大规模线性规划的自适应神经加速
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种用于大规模线性规划的神经加速器，通过预测步长和优化迭代次数，显著提高求解效率。在涉及资产组合优化和风险管理的金融应用中，该技术能大幅减少计算时间，提升高频决策能力。

title: FIDES-Live: Evaluating Behavioral Concordance in Sequential Trading Agents
summary: Sequential trading agents produce decisions, orders, execution receipts, account states, and reports that need not agree, even when the final portfolio value is correctly computed. We present FIDES-Live, an operational extension of FIDES from generated strategy concordance to the audit of sequential agent traces. The protocol separates structured decision validity, optional numerical commitment adherence, execution and ledger reconciliation, and receipt- grounded reporting, with explicit coverage and unscorable outcomes. We retrospectively audit ten requested inference routes over 7,299 cryptocurrency account-rounds and a 310-round equity pilot, using real market observations and local paper execution. Cryptocurrency decision validity is 97.35% and structured reporting accuracy is 90.81% among scorable responses, but route-level decision and reporting performance can diverge sharply. Commitment adherence is 94.36% overall; it falls to 62.63% on constraints emitted with nonempty order proposals, compared with 97.56% for valid empty proposals. All retained cash and position transitions reconcile with recorded fills, while execution controls and unavailable quotes explain separate rejection populations. Short-window marked returns provide descriptive context rather than a new test of whether concordance predicts alpha. These observations motivate reporting concordance, evidence coverage, activity, and financial outcomes separately. They do not establish long-run trading skill, semantic faithfulness of explanations, or causal benefits from audit feedback.
core_methodology: FIDES-Live is an operational protocol for auditing sequential trading agents, focusing on decision validity, numerical commitment adherence, execution reconciliation, and receipt-grounded reporting. It evaluates behavioral concordance in trading agents by separating structured decision validity from execution and ledger reconciliation.
data_sources: The study uses real market observations and local paper execution across 7,299 cryptocurrency account-rounds and a 310-round equity pilot.
alpha_potential: The paper does not directly establish alpha generation but provides a framework for ensuring trading agents' decisions and executions are concordant, which could indirectly improve strategy reliability and performance. The high decision validity (97.35%) and structured reporting accuracy (90.81%) suggest potential for reducing operational risks in automated trading.
title_cn: FIDES-Live：评估顺序交易代理的行为一致性
summary_cn: FIDES-Live 是一种用于审计顺序交易代理的操作协议，重点关注决策有效性、数值承诺遵守、执行对账和基于收据的报告。该研究通过分离结构化决策有效性与执行和账本对账，评估了交易代理的行为一致性。虽然未直接证明阿尔法生成，但高决策有效性（97.35%）和结构化报告准确性（90.81%）表明可能降低自动化交易中的操作风险。

title: Recall or Relearn? A Mixture of In-Context Experts for Recurring Concept Drift
summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are being applied to Web data streams such as network intrusion detection, where they adapt by updating the labelled rows of their context without retraining. When a past concept returns after leaving the context, a TFM faces a recall-or-relearn decision between restoring stored rows of the concept and relearning it from new labels. We propose MICE (Mixture of In-Context Experts), a training-free learner that cuts the stream into segments at detected changes. It merges a closed segment into a stored context when the TFM's estimated additional error on the segment is within a tolerance, under a capacity limit on stored contexts. A fast level weights the stored contexts and first-in-first-out (FIFO) windows by the log-loss of their predictions on the last labelled batch. We show that, with pure stored contexts and a margin condition, this fast level gains over relearning, in expected accuracy, the normalised positive area between the stored context's accuracy and the TFM's learning curve, up to a first-batch term. A slow level mixes the fast level's prediction with that of the FIFO window of the last labelled rows and bounds the discounted half-Brier regret of MICE against this window at every time. Learning curves measured beforehand predict the ordering of the observed recall gains. MICE outperforms reset, which empties the context at detected drifts, on grid streams with random boundary phases. Merging keeps fewer experts than pools that store every segment, and with fixed segmentation a time-matched snapshot pool matches MICE on the shifted grid. On real streams, MICE has the highest mean accuracy of all policies we compare.
core_methodology: MICE (Mixture of In-Context Experts) is a training-free learner that adapts to concept drift by segmenting data streams and merging segments into stored contexts when error tolerance is met, using a weighted combination of stored contexts and FIFO windows.
data_sources: Potentially applicable to financial data streams where concept drift occurs, such as in algorithmic trading or market microstructure analysis.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to adapt to recurring concept drifts without retraining could be valuable in trading strategies that need to handle shifting market regimes or changing correlations between assets.
title_cn: 回忆还是再学习？用于循环概念漂移的上下文专家混合方法
summary_cn: MICE是一种无训练学习器，通过检测数据流变化并合并满足误差容忍度的段到存储上下文中，使用加权组合的存储上下文和FIFO窗口来适应概念漂移，适用于金融数据流中的市场状态变化处理。

title: RankFormer: Rethinking Time Series Transformers through Representation Capacity Analysis and Progressive Decoding
summary: Multivariate time series forecasting plays a critical role in Web and cyber-physical systems, where large-scale services and IoT infrastructures generate complex temporal data. Transformer-based models have achieved strong empirical performance in this domain, yet the principles governing the expressive capacity of their learned representations remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, many existing models rely on simplified decoding strategies, including channel-independent modeling and direct projection heads, which limit their ability to capture complex multivariate dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose RankFormer, a novel encoder-decoder architecture for multivariate time series forecasting. We establish a rank-based analysis framework to investigate how tokenization, embedding, and attention designs affect the representation capacity of time series Transformers. Our analysis reveals that patchification increases the potential representation capacity by aggregating multiple temporal observations into each token, while subsequent encoding operations determine how much of this capacity is realized. Guided by these insights, we develop a rank-enhancing encoder with Hourglass Attention to improve rank stability during information interaction. Furthermore, we introduce the Interactive Progressive Decoder (IPD), which improves future trajectory modeling through global-guided cross-channel interaction and progressive refinement. Extensive experiments on real-world long-term forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that RankFormer achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods. Code repository: https://github.com/TangPeiwang/Rankformer.
core_methodology: The paper proposes RankFormer, a novel encoder-decoder architecture for multivariate time series forecasting. It introduces a rank-based analysis framework to understand the representation capacity of time series Transformers and develops a rank-enhancing encoder with Hourglass Attention and an Interactive Progressive Decoder (IPD) for improved forecasting.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on general multivariate time series forecasting, which could be applied to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to identify patterns in financial time series data, such as stock prices or economic indicators, to generate predictive signals. The improved representation capacity and decoding strategies might enhance the accuracy of financial forecasts.
title_cn: RankFormer：通过表征能力分析和渐进式解码重新思考时间序列Transformer模型
summary_cn: 本文提出了RankFormer，一种用于多元时间序列预测的新型编码器-解码器架构。通过排名分析框架，研究了Token化、嵌入和注意力设计对时间序列Transformer表征能力的影响。引入了Hourglass Attention和交互式渐进解码器（IPD）以提高预测性能。该方法可应用于金融时间序列预测，通过改进的表征能力和解码策略生成更准确的交易信号。

title: Conservative Dueling Bandits: Preference Learning under Baseline Constraints
summary: Contextual dueling bandits learn from pairwise comparisons, the same feedback used to fine-tune language models from human preferences. Standard algorithms explore aggressively and can show users two poor options. We study conservative contextual dueling bandits, which require that, at every round, the cumulative score of the better displayed item stay above a $(1-\alpha)$ fraction of a trusted baseline's. An item's score is its probability of beating the best available item, so the constraint depends only on utility differences and needs no absolute rewards. This also changes how safety can be certified: we show that transferring the safety test of the conservative bandit algorithm CLUCB unchanged can incur linear regret, even when the baseline's utilities are known exactly. For linear utilities, we develop MaxInP-BC, which certifies scores through utility gaps and, when it must fall back, pairs the baseline with an informative partner so that fallback rounds still drive learning. It is safe with high probability at all times, with regret $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{T}/\kappa)$ plus an additive cost of conservatism that does not grow with the horizon. For general utility classes, we develop BTIGW-BC, which turns the guarantee of an online logistic-regression oracle into cumulative safety certificates. It is safe at all times, makes finitely many fallbacks, and has sublinear regret whenever the oracle's logistic regret is sublinear. In experiments, both satisfy the constraint, which their unconstrained counterparts often violate, at a moderate cost in regret.
core_methodology: Conservative contextual dueling bandits learning with safety constraints, using pairwise comparisons and utility gap certification
data_sources: Pairwise preference comparisons (similar to human feedback used in RLHF), no specific market data mentioned but methodology applicable to trading scenario comparisons
alpha_potential: Potential for adaptive portfolio optimization under risk constraints where pair comparisons between assets could determine optimal allocations while maintaining safety limits
title_cn: 保守型对决赌博机：基线约束下的偏好学习
summary_cn: 本研究提出的保守型对决赌博机算法通过带安全约束的成对比较学习，适用于需要维持基准绩效的交易场景（如限制回撤下的组合优化）。算法保证任何时刻的累积效用不低于基准线的(1-α)比例，并通过效用差认证实现安全探索。在金融领域可应用于风险约束下的动态资产选择等问题。

title: LLM knowledge for improved Out-of-Distribution Tabular Prediction - A Cross-Validated Regularisation Approach
summary: Prediction models degrade when the deployment population differs from the one used to train them, and training data cannot say which feature-response relationships will transfer. Expert elicitation is slow and unscalable. We ask whether coefficient priors elicited from large language models (LLMs) improve out-of-distribution (OOD) prediction as the shrinkage target of a regularised regression instead of zero, across five tabular datasets split on real covariates, selecting providers and prior structures by source-domain cross-validation alone. The priors help on four of five datasets, by up to 7.9% OOD mean squared error, and ten of twenty-four prior-informed results resolve the mean improvement at conventional confidence; single-deployment intervals are much wider. On classification the gain is in probabilistic accuracy, not ranking, and control tests with corrupted priors attribute the benefit to feature-specific content rather than scale. Two findings temper this. Variation across candidate priors exceeds the average benefit, yet cross-validation margins fall below their own noise, so selection avoids the worst prior rather than finding the best. On three datasets the prior improves in-domain accuracy as much as out-of-domain, making it better regularisation than shift correction. Only where the training data are large enough that the in-domain gain disappears does elicited knowledge demonstrably improve transfer. Code, priors and results: https://github.com/hugohammer/llm-priors-ood.
core_methodology: The paper proposes using coefficient priors elicited from large language models (LLMs) as shrinkage targets in regularized regression to improve out-of-distribution (OOD) prediction. The approach is validated across five tabular datasets, with performance measured using cross-validation.
data_sources: The study uses five tabular datasets split on real covariates, though the specific nature of these datasets (financial or otherwise) is not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The method shows promise in improving prediction accuracy when deployment conditions differ from training, which could be valuable in financial markets where data distributions often shift. However, the applicability to financial data specifically is not explicitly tested.
title_cn: 利用LLM知识改进分布外表格预测——一种交叉验证正则化方法
summary_cn: 该研究通过从大型语言模型（LLM）中提取系数先验，作为正则化回归的收缩目标，以提高分布外（OOD）预测的准确性。在五个表格数据集上的实验表明，该方法在四个数据集上提升了OOD预测性能，平均平方误差降低高达7.9%。这一技术可能适用于金融市场中数据分布变化的情况，但具体在金融数据上的效果仍需验证。

title: ReForest: Interpretability Meets Reasoning in Isolation Forest
summary: Statistical anomaly detection methods like Isolation Forest are efficient but suffer from a critical semantic gap. They identify numerical rarities but fail to understand the contextual meaning of data, often missing subtle, context-dependent anomalies. Conversely, Large Language Models possess strong semantic reasoning capabilities but are prohibitively expensive and slow for large-scale deployment. To bridge this gap, we propose ReForest, a novel framework that synergizes the statistical efficiency of Isolation Forest with the reasoning power of LLMs. ReForest transforms the latent decision paths of Isolation Forest into natural-language explanations, enabling an LLM to refine anomaly detection through an uncertainty-aware dynamic ensemble. This approach allows the model to adaptively weigh statistical and semantic signals based on uncertainty-driven instance-level confidence. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets (Healthcare, Finance) demonstrate that ReForest significantly outperforms baselines, achieving an average 21% improvement in Recall and a 10% gain in F1-score. Our framework not only improves detection performance but also enhances model transparency by grounding semantic narratives in statistical evidence, providing interpretable rationales essential for high-stakes decision-making.
core_methodology: ReForest combines Isolation Forest's statistical anomaly detection with LLMs' semantic reasoning to improve anomaly detection through natural-language explanations and uncertainty-aware dynamic ensemble.
data_sources: Real-world datasets including Finance, indicating potential application to financial data such as market anomalies or fraud detection.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify subtle, context-dependent anomalies in financial data that traditional methods might miss, particularly useful for detecting market manipulation, fraud, or unusual trading patterns.
title_cn: ReForest：孤立森林的解释性与推理能力结合
summary_cn: ReForest将孤立森林的统计异常检测与大型语言模型的语义推理能力相结合，通过自然语言解释和不确定性感知的动态集成，显著提升了异常检测的召回率和F1分数。该方法在金融领域可应用于市场异常或欺诈检测，识别传统方法可能遗漏的细微、上下文相关的异常。

title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
summary: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. Furthermore, our design offers flexibility for resource-constrained environments, supporting selective modality encoder loading, adjustable vision token budgets, truncatable embedding dimensions, and quantized weights. We present ablations analyzing key decisions and release EmbeddingGemma 2 to promote further research.
core_methodology: Unified multimodal embedding model for text, images, audio, and video with optimized efficiency features like selective modality loading and quantized weights
data_sources: Not finance-specific, but capable of processing alternative data sources used in trading (e.g., earnings call transcripts, satellite images, financial videos)
alpha_potential: Potential for extracting signals from multimodal financial data (e.g., combining text sentiment with visual chart patterns), though requires custom financial domain adaptation
title_cn: EmbeddingGemma 2：统一高效的多模态表征模型
summary_cn: 该论文提出的多模态嵌入模型可用于处理金融领域的文本、图像等异构数据，如结合财报文本与股价图表进行联合分析。模型的效率优化特征（如选择性模态加载）适合高频量化场景，但需针对金融数据特性进行定制化适配。

title: TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling
summary: Ant International accumulates large volumes of transaction history across users and payment businesses. Confirmed fraud and chargeback outcomes, by contrast, are scarce, delayed, and specific to each business. A single encoder pretrained on unlabeled histories could serve all businesses, but only if pretraining captures the behavior that separates risk. Coarse activity differences can make contrastive pretraining on transaction logs too easy: transaction volume, amount, and timing can distinguish a history's continuation from arbitrary candidates without modeling how payment resources are used. We present TRIDENT-Seq, a transaction foundation model trained with Prefix-Future Contrast (PFC). PFC matches each prefix to a summary of its subsequent behavior among candidates with similar activity profiles; activity prediction and dispersion regularization act on the encoder output. Across three production payment businesses, the pretrained encoder improves average precision (AP) and recall at a 0.5% intervention budget over architecture-matched scratch training in all six business-budget settings. With a fixed validation set, it exceeds full-label scratch training in mean AP and recall using 10% of the training labels on Wallet and 25% on Shopping and SME. Pretraining only on another business's histories still helps. Replacing profile-matched candidates with random ones cuts recall from 24.62% to 5.64%. In Ant International's deployment evaluation, recorded amount-based chargeback and overall loss rates are 37.7% and 37.9% lower than those of the previous XGBoost-based system under the same intervention budget.
core_methodology: TRIDENT-Seq uses a transaction foundation model trained with Prefix-Future Contrast (PFC), which matches transaction prefixes to summaries of subsequent behavior among similar activity profiles. It incorporates activity prediction and dispersion regularization to improve encoder performance.
data_sources: Transaction histories from Ant International's payment businesses, including user payment behaviors and fraud/chargeback outcomes.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to predict payment risk and fraud more accurately than traditional methods like XGBoost suggests potential for improving risk management and fraud detection in trading and financial applications, especially in environments with limited labeled data.
title_cn: TRIDENT-Seq：基于行为匹配前缀未来对比的支付风险建模标签高效方法
summary_cn: TRIDENT-Seq通过前缀未来对比（PFC）训练交易基础模型，有效识别支付风险行为，尤其在标签数据稀缺的情况下。在蚂蚁国际的实际部署中，较传统XGBoost系统显著降低了37.9%的损失率，展示了在金融风控和高频交易风险管理的应用潜力。

title: Test-Time Communication in Trading Agent Swarms
summary: Communication between agents has mostly been studied on tasks with a shared objective and fast, clear feedback. Trading has neither: each agent manages its own account, with decisions being scored by markets late and noisily. A trading swarm is thus a population of independent decision-makers rather than a team, for which convergence is a risk and not the goal. We ran 200 agents from four model families in groups of ten under five communication regimes, from isolation to message boards and shared notes, over seven US trading days (1 to 9 October 2026), logging everything each agent read before every decision. In two of the four families, communicating groups came to hold far more of the same stocks than the isolated group. A group's return was largely the return on what its members held in common. Seeing a post from a groupmate made an agent 7 percentage points more likely to reuse an eight-word phrase from it. Agents that started too close together to see each other's posts shared such a phrase in 14% of cases, the rate that common inputs produce. Seeing the post did not detectably change that morning's trades. Case studies traced the adoption of positions and decision rules over subsequent days, and communicating groups sold in step more often than isolated ones. Because isolated groups also converged on the same stocks, sometimes completely, assessments of herding need to measure excess convergence relative to a no-peer baseline.
core_methodology: The paper studies communication effects in agent-based trading systems using controlled experiments with 200 agents across four model families under five communication regimes. It analyzes how information sharing impacts trading convergence and performance metrics.
data_sources: Experimental data from simulated US trading environments over seven trading days (1-9 October 2026). Includes detailed logs of agent decisions, message content, and portfolio holdings.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify informational alpha from agent communication patterns. Highlights how peer influence affects portfolio concentration and trade synchronization, suggesting ways to detect emergent herding behavior before market impacts.
title_cn: 交易智能体群组的测试时通信研究
summary_cn: 该论文通过200个交易智能体在5种通信机制下的实验，揭示了同伴通信如何导致持仓趋同和交易同步。研究发现：1) 通信组持仓集中度显著提高 2) 观察到同伴消息会使智能体重复使用短语概率增加7% 3) 需建立基线区分自然趋同和同伴影响。这对量化监测市场羊群行为和开发反共识策略具有启示。

title: Interpretable Meta-Policies for Neural Decision Making
summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning remains difficult to interpret and align due to the black-box nature of neural networks. While (neuro-)symbolic approaches improve transparency by incorporating symbolic reasoning, applying them directly to low-level actions results in overly complex, unreadable policies. We introduce NEXUS, a hierarchical RL framework that resolves this tension by combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies. By shifting transparent reasoning to high-level skills rather than atomic actions, NEXUS drastically reduces symbolic complexity without sacrificing environment performance. Object-centric observations enable high-level reasoning and the design of reward functions and meta-policies by interaction with LLMs. We demonstrate that NEXUS agents learn disentangled skills, are interpretable regarding high-level goals, are better aligned to goals described in the game manual, less prone to reward hacking and more robust to game simplifications than deep RL. Finally, we isolate and evaluate the impact of different meta-policy architectures (neural, symbolic, neuro-symbolic) on environmental return and aligned task performance.
core_methodology: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning combining neural skills with symbolic meta-policies for interpretable decision-making
data_sources: Object-centric observations (simulated environment in paper, but potentially applicable to market state representations)
alpha_potential: Could improve algorithmic trading by creating more interpretable and aligned trading strategies that are less prone to reward hacking in complex market environments
title_cn: 神经决策的可解释元策略
summary_cn: NEXUS框架通过结合神经技能与符号元策略，创建层次化强化学习系统，提升决策可解释性。在量化交易中，该方法有助于开发更透明、与市场目标更一致的交易策略，减少奖励作弊风险，尤其适用于复杂市场环境中的算法决策优化。

title: GTFormer: A Syntax-Free Graph Network Alternative to Transformers for 8192$\times$ Length Extrapolation in Linear Time
summary: Self-attention mechanisms have established the Transformer as the dominant backbone across natural language processing, source code intelligence, and automated theorem proving. However, all-to-all pairwise token comparison enforces a quadratic $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ compute and memory barrier alongside severe softmax attention dilution as sequence length $N$ scales beyond the training horizon. Inspired by recent advances in algebraic graph learning (\textbf{WPNet}), this work introduces \textbf{GTFormer}, a syntax-free hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) that replaces flat self-attention for general long-context sequence modeling. GTFormer organizes raw token streams into a bounded-degree hierarchy combining a balanced binary reduction tree ($\lceil \log_2 N \rceil$ depth), horizontal boundary-bridging shift edges, random expander shortcuts, multi-channel convex highway gating, and a top-down broadcast pass. Across eight long-context code, log, and multi-hop retrieval benchmarks trained exclusively on sequences of length $N \le 512$, GTFormer extrapolates zero-shot to $N = 4{,}194{,}304$ ($8192\times$) on a single commodity GPU in linear $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, maintaining near-perfect accuracy where standard and RoPE Transformers suffer from out-of-distribution attention collapse and out-of-memory exhaustion.
core_methodology: GTFormer introduces a hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) as an alternative to Transformers, focusing on long-context sequence modeling with linear time and memory complexity. It organizes token streams into a bounded-degree hierarchy with features like balanced binary reduction trees, boundary-bridging edges, random expander shortcuts, and multi-channel highway gating.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general long-context sequences, potentially applicable to financial time-series data, logs, and other structured or unstructured data in trading environments.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be valuable for processing long financial time-series or high-frequency data efficiently, potentially uncovering patterns or signals that traditional Transformers might miss due to their quadratic complexity. However, the paper does not specifically address financial applications, so adaptation is required.
title_cn: GTFormer：一种无语法图网络替代Transformer的线性时间8192倍长度外推方法
summary_cn: GTFormer提出了一种层次化图神经网络（GNN）替代Transformer，专注于长上下文序列建模，具有线性时间和内存复杂度。该方法可高效处理金融时间序列或高频数据，潜在揭示传统Transformer因二次复杂度而忽略的信号，但需进一步适配金融应用。

title: TeamGym: A Gym for Team Decision-Making by AI Agents with Distributed Information
summary: Many real-world decisions require teams to integrate information distributed across participants. Yet AI agents are still primarily trained and benchmarked in isolation. We introduce TeamGym, an environment for evaluating and training language model-based agents on team decision-making problems constructed from real-world legal, finance, medical, and software engineering corpora. TeamGym introduces a method to identify a minimal set of facts, each element of which is necessary and all of which are collectively sufficient for a correct final decision, which we call pivotal information. This enables TeamGym to both control the distribution of pivotal information and track how well agents identify and integrate pivotal information when making team decisions. Examining 8 language models on 12 source corpora, we find that current AI agents often fail to effectively share information: Distributing pivotal information across participants lowers success rate by 22.9 percentage points on average relative to giving the same information to a single model (a communication gap). We also document that participants do not effectively retrieve decision-relevant information on their own: A team's success rate is lowered by a further 19.9 points when participants must identify and extract pivotal information from source material rather than receiving it directly (a retrieval gap). To help remedy these deficits, we use TeamGym to train policies through reinforcement learning on team decision loss. Across two policy-training experiments, we find that training improves final-decision quality and induces emergent coordination in participation, speaker selection, and communication, even though the reward evaluates only the final decision.
core_methodology: Environment for evaluating and training language model-based agents on team decision-making problems, with a focus on identifying and integrating pivotal information using reinforcement learning.
data_sources: Real-world legal, finance, medical, and software engineering corpora.
alpha_potential: Potential applications in distributed decision-making scenarios in trading, such as multi-agent systems for portfolio management or arbitrage strategies where information is distributed across different sources or agents.
title_cn: TeamGym：一种用于具有分布式信息的AI代理团队决策的训练环境
summary_cn: 该论文提出了TeamGym环境，专注于基于语言模型的代理在团队决策中的应用，适用于金融等领域的分布式决策场景。通过强化学习训练代理以更好地识别和整合关键信息，虽非直接面向交易策略设计，但可拓展至交易团队或多代理系统中，以提高决策质量和协调效率。

title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
summary: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology.
